decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January indicates that the labor market remains strong but that growth of economic activity has slowed from its solid rate in the fourth quarter.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that while jobs are still strong, overall economic growth has cooled down since the end of last year.

changes.quote: Payroll employment was little changed in February, but job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: Job growth slowed in February, but the average trend remains solid and unemployment is low.

changes.quote: Recent indicators point to slower growth of household spending and business fixed investment in the first quarter.
changes.explanation: Consumers and businesses are spending and investing at a slower pace in the early part of the year.

changes.quote: On a 12-month basis, overall inflation has declined, largely as a result of lower energy prices; inflation for items other than food and energy remains near 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Lower energy costs pulled overall annual inflation down, while core inflation stays close to the 2 percent target.

changes.quote: On balance, market-based measures of inflation compensation have remained low in recent months, and survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed.
changes.explanation: Measures of future inflation expectations in markets and surveys remain stable and low.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee continues to view sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective as the most likely outcomes.

In light of global economic and financial developments and muted inflation pressures, the Committee will be patient as it determines what future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate may be appropriate to support these outcomes.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.73% APR costs about $61.38 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.54% and moved -7 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.41% would fall by about $12.39 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.8%, and employers added an average of 150k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.5% over the past year (February 2019); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -6 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.29%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.07% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will remain patient and take time to assess economic conditions before making any changes to interest rates. An educational forecast model suggests a 97% chance of a hold at the next meeting.

citations.detail: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent.
